title: The Jobs of Tomorrow
text:
Many workers today worry that automation will replace their jobs. However, a recent report suggests that new roles will appear faster than old ones disappear. Employers are already looking for people who can work with data, communicate clearly, and adapt to new tools. For this reason, universities are beginning to offer short courses that focus on practical skills rather than only theory.

Career advisers recommend that young people build a portfolio of projects instead of relying only on a diploma. A portfolio shows what a person can actually do, which is often more convincing to employers. Advisers also suggest that workers keep learning throughout their lives, because the skills needed in five years may be different from those needed today.

questions.text: According to the report, how will new roles compare with old ones?
options: They will disappear faster than old ones.
They will appear faster than old ones disappear.
They will not appear at all.
They will be created only by universities.

questions.text: What do career advisers recommend that young people build?
What can be inferred about employers from the passage?
options: They value practical abilities over formal qualifications alone.
They prefer workers who never change jobs.
They have stopped hiring people with diplomas.
They believe automation has no effect on work.

questions.text: Why do career advisers stress lifelong learning?
options: Because jobs will stay the same for decades.
Because the skills needed in the future may change.
Because diplomas are no longer valid.
Because young people cannot learn quickly.

paragraph_translations: Muchos trabajadores hoy temen que la automatización reemplace sus empleos. Sin embargo, un informe reciente sugiere que los nuevos puestos aparecerán más rápido de lo que desaparecen los antiguos. Los empleadores ya buscan personas que sepan trabajar con datos, comunicarse con claridad y adaptarse a nuevas herramientas. Por esta razón, las universidades empiezan a ofrecer cursos breves centrados en habilidades prácticas y no solo en la teoría.

Los asesores de carrera recomiendan que los jóvenes construyan un portafolio de proyectos en lugar de depender solo de un título. Un portafolio muestra lo que una persona puede hacer realmente, lo cual suele resultar más convincente para los empleadores. Los asesores también sugieren que los trabajadores sigan aprendiendo durante toda la vida, porque las habilidades necesarias dentro de cinco años pueden ser diferentes de las actuales.
